messages.subject: Help me isolate()
parts:
Shinyfiers,

I've built an app that's grown quite complex, with multiple tabs, each tab with it's own inputs, etc.  Everything is reactive to inputs in my sidebar and the individual panels, which slows things down a lot.

But I want the inputs in my sidebar to NOT trigger changes immediately.  i.e., I want those inputs tied submitbutton, and all other inputs in the tabs to be reactive.  I tried having a submit button, but by default all inputs in the whole app were tied to it, which was a really bad experience.

Maybe I'm just slow, but the concept of isolate() is not making sense.  So could someone please just tell me what to do in this case?  How can one form have a submit button and everything else be reactive?

Cheers
John

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: Help me isolate()
parts:
I am quite newb and I haven't use the submit button much. I find action button a bit better. 

Try actionButton in the ui.R in place of a submit button.

Say you name your actionButton myBtn then input$myBtn will increment by 1 everytime you press it. So now put everything that can the results into an isolate.

Eg.

observe({
  if(input$myBtn >0 ) {
     something <- isolate(input$someControl)
     dosomething(something)
  }
})

Make sure everything other than input$myBtn is wrapped in isolate.
